ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on the Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Information (Act No. 18619, effective March 23, 2021) and its Enforcement Decree; Financial Transaction Reports Act (Act No. 18620); Commercial Act (Act No. 17905) as amended, particularly Article 342-2 regarding beneficial ownership disclosure; and the Act on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism (Act No. 18621).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For documents originating from Hague Apostille Convention member states: Notarize at local notary, then obtain Apostille from the competent authority (e.g., Secretary of State in the US). For non-member states: Notarize, then legalize at the Korean Embassy/Consulate in the country of origin, followed by authentication by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Same as above: Apostille for member states; Consular legalization for non-member states.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney (이사회 결의서 / 위임장)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the resolution, then obtain Apostille (member states) or consular legalization (non-member states).
Notarize the articles, then Apostille or consular legalization as applicable.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank (must be a licensed financial institution)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letter must be notarized, then Apostille or consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) designated list. Additionally, all beneficial owners, directors, and senior officers must undergo enhanced due diligence (EDD) for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) and the Korean AML Act. Screening must be conducted at onboarding and continuously on a real-time basis using automated systems. Any positive match triggers immediate suspension of the incorporation process and filing of a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) with KoFIU within 24 hours. The compliance officer must document all screening results and maintain records for at least 5 years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Registry (Court Registration System) - www.iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Korean (Hangul) as the primary legal name. An English name may be registered as a secondary name but must be a phonetic transliteration of the Korean name or a direct translation. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered company in Korea. The name must include a corporate suffix such as '주식회사' (Chusik Hoesa) or '유한회사' (Yuhan Hoesa). For foreign entities, the name must be transliterated into Hangul according to the Korean Language and Alphabet Standardization Act.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Court Registry within 30 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must be submitted in writing, stating the grounds for reconsideration, and must include a proposed alternative name. The registry will review the appeal within 15 business days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may file a lawsuit with the Administrative Court within 30 days. Alternatively, the applicant may submit a new name application immediately. The appeal process does not extend the reservation period; therefore, it is advisable to reserve a backup name simultaneously.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices and commercial mailboxes are generally not accepted for corporate registration in South Korea. The Commercial Act requires a physical registered office where the company's management and records are maintained. For tax purposes, the National Tax Service (NTS) requires a physical address for business registration and VAT purposes. Banks also require a physical office for opening corporate accounts and for AML/KYC compliance. For the gaming industry, the Korean Game Rating and Administration Committee (GRAC) may require a physical presence for licensing. Therefore, a virtual office is not permissible for this entity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: The Korean tax authorities (NTS) and the Court Registry conduct periodic and unannounced physical inspections. The likelihood is moderate (30-40%) for newly incorporated companies, especially those in the digital content sector. Inspections may verify the existence of the registered office, presence of employees, and compliance with commercial substance requirements. The checklist includes: (1) physical signage with company name, (2) dedicated office space, (3) presence of corporate records and accounting books, (4) availability of management personnel, (5) evidence of business operations (e.g., server logs, contracts). Failure to pass an inspection can result in fines, revocation of registration, and adverse tax consequences.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (상법), Act No. 1001, as amended, particularly Articles 288 (incorporation), 289 (articles of incorporation), 291 (subscription of shares), 292 (promoters' subscription), 295 (payment obligations), 296 (payment by deposit into designated bank), 317 (registration of incorporation), 350 (issuance of shares), 363 (calls of shareholders' general meeting), 382 (appointment of directors), 383 (number of directors, at least three or one for small company under Article 383(1) proviso), 393 (board of directors' authority), 415 (statutory auditors) and Article 542(2) metric: 0
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registry Division, Seoul District Court (법원행정처 등기국 / 서울중앙지방법원 등기과) operating under the Supreme Court of Korea's Registration Act and the Korea Trade Information Service (KOTRA) for foreign investment notification
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (정관) together with Certificate of Incorporation Application (회사설립등기신청서) and written share subscription forms (주식청약서) filed under Article 317 of the Commercial Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None (no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa in Korea). The obligation is simply that the consideration for issued shares be actually and fully paid or contributed before incorporation, typically by depositing the subscribed amount into a designated bank account in the name of the promoter(s) or a special incorporation account. The paid-up amount may be as low as KRW 1 per share and need not be blocked after incorporation; however, amounts deposited before incorporation are released only upon presentation of the registration certificate or a certificate of deposit, and the company may freely use the funds once registered. Foreign investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act must file a foreign-investment report with KOTRA before payment if the investment exceeds KRW 100 million or involves foreign exchange acquisition.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME], A CHUSIK HOESA ORGANIZED UNDER THE LAWS OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA, ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE SOLE/ALL DIRECTORS AS OF [DATE OF INCORPORATION]. WHEREAS, the Company was duly incorporated under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (the Commercial Act) on [Date], with the issuance of [number] ordinary shares to its initial shareholders; WHEREAS, the initial directors of the Company, being the directors named in the Articles of Incorporation, are authorized and required to take all actions necessary to organize the Company and to enable it to commence lawful business; WHEREAS, the Company intends to elect its first representative director, appoint its statutory auditor, adopt its corporate seal and banking resolutions, and designate its registered office. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED: 1. That the shares issued in connection with the incorporation of the Company, consisting of [number] ordinary shares with a par value of KRW [amount] each, are hereby ratified and confirmed, and the aggregate subscription consideration of KRW [amount] paid into the designated deposit account in the name of [Promoter Bank] is acknowledged as having been fully paid in compliance with Articles 295, 296 and 317 of the Commercial Act. 2. That the registered office of the Company shall be at [full address], and the appropriate local registry of the competent court shall be notified of such office; the Representative Director is authorized to make any necessary amendments to the corporate register. 3. That [Name] be and hereby is elected and appointed as the Representative Director (대표이사) of the Company with full authority to represent the Company in all affairs, to execute contracts, to open and operate bank accounts, to file all governmental permits and registrations, and to act alone unless otherwise limited by the Board. 4. That [Name] be and hereby is appointed as the statutory auditor (감사) of the Company, being qualified under Article 410 of the Commercial Act, to audit the accounting records and monitor the legality of management. 5. That the corporate seal of the Company, as affixed to the Articles of Incorporation and stored at the registered office, be adopted, and the Representative Director shall file the identical seal notification under Article 24 of the Framework Act on Electronic Documents and Transactions for e-seal registration. 6. That the Company shall open accounts with [Bank Name], with the Representative Director, jointly with [CFO/Finance Director], as the authorized signatories; the bank has received this resolution and may rely upon it until written revocation. 7. That the initial fiscal year end shall be [December 31] and the Representative Director shall cause all required filings under the Commercial Act and the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies to be prepared. 8. That all actions taken by the promoters, directors and officers in the negotiation, execution and delivery of contracts, applications for business licenses, and filings with the competent authorities are ratified and confirmed. 9. That the Representative Director be authorized to execute all documents, pay all fees, and undertake all steps necessary to implement the foregoing resolutions and to comply with the laws of the Republic of Korea and any jurisdiction in which the Company operates. 10. That these resolutions shall be effective immediately and shall be recorded in the minutes of the first board meeting and filed in the Company's statutory records. ADOPTED AND APPROVED this [day] day of [month], [year].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Korean-language pre-incorporation name check and articles of incorporation drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Information Center (인터넷등기소) and any local notary public authorized by the Korean Notary Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The promoters must first reserve the Korean corporate name through the Supreme Court registry portal by verifying against identical or confusingly similar existing names of Chusik Hoesa entities. The name must contain the word 주식회사 (Chusik Hoesa) or be clearly identifiable as a stock corporation. Concurrently, the promoters must prepare the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation satisfying Commercial Act Article 289, stating objectives, company name, total authorized shares, par value, registered office address, method of public notice, promotion and share-subscription schedules issued to the founders. If any foreign national or foreign corporation subscribes to shares, the subscription documents must be prepared in Korean and English and the proposed investment must be reported to KOTRA under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before deposit of consideration. The articles must be notarized by a Korean notary public who will verify the promoters' identity and sign the certificate of notarization. The articles shall list subscribers, number of shares subscribed, paid-in amount and stated capital. All documents must be executed with original Korean seal attestations or notarized signatures.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (정관) drafted in Korean
Certificate of seal impression of each promoter/founder
Identity documents and power of attorney of each promoter (passport or foreigner ID)
Foreign investment report (for foreign investors, issued by KOTRA) or waiver exemption statement
Proposed company name search certificate or reservation receipt issued by the Registry Information Center
List of directors, auditor and representative director candidates with consent forms accepting appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses to notarize or the registry rejects the proposed name, the promoters may correct the articles and re-submitted application. After obtaining a written deficiency notice from the notary or registry, the promoter shall remedy the missing or defective items within two weeks; if the refusal is based on confusing similarity of name, choose up to three alternate reserved names and re-confirm availability. A registrar remedying order may be cured by filing corrected particulars against the same receipt within five business days, failing which the filing is deemed void and all fees refunded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription and capital deposit into a designated financial institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The financial institution designated as a domestic bank in the name of the promoter or the company (e.g., Hana Bank, Woori Bank, Shinhan Bank) and the Foreign Investment Support Center of KOTRA for any foreign investment report
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Where shares are subscribed for cash, the promoters must open a temporary or designated deposit account and pay the total subscription price to that account in accordance with Commercial Act Article 295 and Article 296. The payment must be made no later than sixty days from the date of subscription or from the effective date of the foreign investment report, whichever is later. Each subscriber must deposit the full amount of subscription, and no set-off or installment payment is permitted. The bank must issue a certificate of deposit (납입증명서) confirming that the funds are held for the subscribed shares. If the incorporation does not proceed to registration, the deposit must be returned to the subscribers unconditionally. Once incorporation registration is completed and a certificate of registration is presented, the funds may be released for corporate purposes. Foreign investors must use a foreign currency or won account and ensure the remittance is supported by the KOTRA report to permit future dividend repatriation. The deposit certificate, together with a bank confirmation of the actual exchange rate and amount, shall be included in the registration application.
required_dossiers: Certificate of deposit of subscription price (납입증명서) issued by the designated bank
Foreign investment notification certificate (from KOTRA) or receipt
Copy of share subscription forms with subscriber addresses, names, and number of shares
Outbound remittance certificate from the foreign investor's bank if invested from outside Korea
Funds source statement / compliance declaration applicable under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
Taxpayer ID number of each corporate subscriber (or certified copy of corporate registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank withholds the deposit certificate or the amount was deposited in an incorrect currency, the promoter must immediately reconcile the account and re-remit amounts. If KOTRA issues a request for supplementary documents on the foreign-investment report, the investor has up to twenty days to provide corrected contracts and bank certificates. When the registered deed is later suspended due to insufficient proof of paid-in capital, the receiving court official may re-inspect the deposit; the remedy is to present a fresh certificate, obtain a stamped statement from the bank that the account remains intact, and refile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation registration filing with the Seoul District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Register of Companies, Seoul District Court (서울중앙지방법원 등기국), with electronic submission through the Supreme Court Internet Registry (인터넷등기소)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the articles have been notarized and the capital deposit verified, the promoters must submit the registration application for incorporation within two weeks of the date of payment of all subscription price. The application must be signed by every promoter or their authorized attorney and must be accompanied by evidence that each director and auditor has accepted office. The registry will assign a corporate registration number, then record the company name, location of the main office, capital amount, annual meeting rules, names of directors/auditors, representative director, and the corporate seal imprint. The local judge will review documents for formal regularity, verify that the paid capital is deposited, and confirm that the statutory requirements of Commercial Act Article 317 have been met. Once accepted, the registry issues a Certificate of Registered Incorporation (등기사항증명서). This step must also include registration of the business commencement date in the corporate registers, and the company must file a notice to the local tax office within twenty days of the registration for corporate income tax domicile.
required_dossiers: Original notarized Articles of Incorporation with notary certificate
Acceptance statements from each representative director, director and statutory auditor
Certificate of deposit of the paid-in capital in the bank account
Certificate of seal impression of the company's corporate seal required for registration
Foreign investment report certificate or visa-related certification for foreign directors
Power of attorney authorizing a local legal professional to effect registration
Pre-registration tax clearance certificate (for the promoter, where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a 'renewal of registration' correction order due to missing evidence or inconsistent article provisions, the applicant must submit a corrective supplement or a written explanation within 15 days of receiving notice. If the registration is refused, an immediate appeal can be filed with the District Court under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act. Any ambiguity in the identity of the representative director is fixed by submitting a separate director's consent and restating the articles of incorporation through a notary. For failure caused by an expired deposit certificate, obtain a new certificate and refile; the date of registration is the date of actual official receipt after correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration, tax authority onboarding, and statutory post-incorporation governance filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office (세무서) under the National Tax Service, the Korea Employment and Labor Service for social insurance registration, and the Registry Information Center for corporate seal notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days of incorporation registration, the representative director must file a business registration application with the tax office that has jurisdiction over the registered office, providing the corporate registration certificate and the company's business scope under ISIC 5820 / KSIC 58210 (software publishing) so that the tax identification and VAT registration is issued. The office will issue a corporate tax number and, after review, a business registration certificate. Concurrently, the company must register the corporate seal with the tax office and with the local district court. The company must then register its chief director, employees and principal place of business with the local labour and social insurance authorities within 14 days for the national pension, employment insurance, industrial accident insurance and health insurance. For a Korean source digital game publisher with global MMORPG operations, the company should prepare a permanent establishment risk and withholding declaration, secure a local game provider license, if any, and complete annual external audit appointment if the company meets the threshold under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies. It should also file an initial balance sheet and capital statement within one month of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate registration (등기사항증명서)
Certificate of corporate seal registration
Articles of incorporation and board resolution appointing directors and representative
Lease contract of the registered office or proof of branch office address
Foreign investor business narratives and shareholding schedule
Application for business registration with detailed ISIC/KSIC code 58210
Bank account opening certificate with the designated bank
Social insurance enrollment list for employees and representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office rejects or delays the business registration due to source-of-funds questions, the company may present the deposit certificate, bank remittance records and KOTRA foreign-investment filing; if the issue persists, an administrative appeal may be filed with the National Tax Tribunal. If the employment insurance registration is queried for missing employee details, correct the submission with all employment agreements and alien registration cards for non-resident staff. A delayed filing of the corporate seal may be remedied by direct submission to the civil registration department along with a late-filing fee, and any defect in the external auditor appointment is cured by appointment at a temporary general shareholders' meeting, followed by amended reporting.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable — the company is classified under ISIC 5820 (software publishing) with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing operations. Digital software publishing of an MMORPG is governed by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and the Korea Game Rating and Administration Committee (게임물관리위원회) under the Game Industry Promotion Act rather than industrial licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable — no industrial operating license, manufacturing permit, or warehouse worksite certificate is required because the registered business performs digital/software publishing activities only. However, the company will undergo voluntary registration and rating classification pursuant to the Game Industry Promotion Act for the platform release of the MMORPG in Korea; such registration is distinct from an industrial physical permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea (유역환경청 / 지방환경청) — Not Applicable to digital-only operations; no physical plant, discharge or relevant environmental receptor.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Pure software publishing / data center-less activities with no EDPS or physical facility will not be subject to prior environmental impact review. If later the company establishes a physical game server warehouse or data center in premises that triggers the Environmental Impact Assessment Act, the classification could become 'Pre-Environmental Review' or 'Full EIA Report' per the scale thresholds of the Act, at which point the project owner must file a plan and undergo scoping.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable — no industrial wastewater, volatile organic compounds, or hazardous waste generated from core MMORPG publishing activity. IT server hosting (cloud) is outsourced and has no physical Korean point-source emission. If equipment were ever operated inside Korea, standards under the Clean Air Conservation Act (atmospheric pollutants: permissible emissions per stack shall be in compliance with Article 16 and enforcement schedule: dust 30 mg/Sm3, sulfur oxides 391 ppm or fewer for daily coal oil, nitrogen oxides 500 ppm and hazardous substances as prescribed) and the Water Quality and Aquatic Ecosystem Conservation Act (biochemical oxygen demand: BOD under 10 mg/L for public wastewater treatment connection, total nitrogen ≤ 60 mg/L, total phosphorus ≤ 8 mg/L) would apply; but for the registered digital scope the answer is Not Applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable — no factory building, warehouse or industrial workplace, so no Civil Defense fire safety certificate for a factory, no structural load approval, and no workplace permit under the Occupational Safety and Health Act is mandated. Should the company open an office of greater than 1,000 square meters or bring a multi-story building under the Act for software work, it would obtain a fire resistance rating and workplace safety report from the National Fire Agency (소방청) and the relevant local fire station; but under the present pure digital/consulting classification, all physical industrial clearance items are Not Applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; primary electronic portal is HomeTax (hometax.go.kr); customs and export clearance are administered by the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS electronic portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Korean-domiciled Chusik Hoesa, file corporate business commencement registration with the District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the registered business address within 20 days from commencement. Access HomeTax using a corporate certificate and submit the business registration application, accompanied by the representative director's identification, articles of incorporation, lease or ownership proof of the place of business, and board resolution if required. The NTS then issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN) that functions as the TIN, VAT registration number, and corporate withholding tax account. Foreign non-resident entities with a domestic place of business must file a foreign corporation business registration with the same district tax office to obtain a BRN. Foreign non-resident electronic service suppliers without a domestic place of business must register through the NTS simplified foreign e-service supplier registration procedure via HomeTax, appoint a Korean tax representative, and obtain a separate foreign operator VAT registration number. Export-active companies must additionally obtain a customs corporate code from the Korea Customs Service.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not provide a check-the-box entity classification election. A Chusik Hoesa is a resident domestic corporation taxed on worldwide income under the Corporate Tax Act and is not a pass-through entity. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are constrained by mandatory anti-hybrid rules under the Corporate Tax Act and the Adjustment of International Taxes Act; there is no elective hybrid-mismatch realignment mechanism.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act, administered by the National Tax Service as a single national indirect tax system with no provincial sales tax overlay.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 (no monetary threshold): every person making taxable supplies in Korea must register for VAT upon business commencement. Individual small-business suppliers with annual revenue below KRW 80,000,000 may elect simplified taxpayer treatment, but a Chusik Hoesa corporation is ineligible and must register as a general VAT taxpayer. Foreign electronic service suppliers (including MMORPG platform and in-app purchase sellers) must VAT-register in Korea regardless of turnover under the NTS simplified foreign electronic service supplier registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices are mandatory for B2B supplies and must be transmitted to the National Tax Service through HomeTax no later than the day after issuance. The NTS operates open APIs for machine-to-machine transmission, and accepts e-invoices after cryptographically validating the Korean business registration number, supply value, VAT amount, and digital signature; an accepted e-invoice carries an NTS validation number that acts as the anti-fraud stamp. Korea does not impose pre-clearance of each invoice before issuance, but the HomeTax system functions as the central fiscal repository and enables real-time risk matching and B2C cash-receipt verification. Failure to issue or transmit an e-invoice in time triggers an additional tax amount equal to 2% of the untaxed supply value.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Value-Added Tax Act, exported goods are zero-rated when physical export is evidenced by a Korea Customs Service export declaration. Services and intangible digital content, including MMORPG global access and in-app purchases delivered through Apple App Store and Google Play distributions, qualify for zero-rating when the recipient is a non-resident, the service is actually used outside Korea, the consideration is paid in foreign currency, and the foreign-exchange proceeds are received and repatriated to Korea. The foreign-exchange earning condition is substantiated by app-store payout statements, bank remittance records, and the corporate accounts showing export consideration. Input VAT paid on costs attributable to zero-rated exports is creditable and refundable if it generates an excess VAT credit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (the Korean export clearance certificate / export bill of entry equivalent) issued by the Korea Customs Service for physical goods
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export movement
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Settlement Confirmation evidencing the arrival of export proceeds in Korea
Commercial invoice and export contract identifying the foreign purchaser, product scope, and payment terms
Apple App Store and Google Play payout/settlement reports together with user geolocation and transaction logs for digital zero-rated supplies
Foreign exchange transaction report from the remitting bank or the Foreign Exchange Information System confirming timely repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating is closely audited by the NTS through cross-matching with Korea Customs Service export declarations, bank remittance data, foreign exchange transaction reports, and app-store settlement files. If the required documentation is incomplete, contradictory, or missing, the 0% rate is retrospectively clawed back and VAT at 10% is assessed on the supply base, plus additional tax for underreporting and for failure to issue/transmit e-invoices. For fraudulent or intentionally unverifiable export zero-rating, the NTS may impose a penalty up to 40% of the VAT evaded, apply the 10-year retrospective assessment period for fraud under the Framework Act on National Taxes, initiate criminal prosecution for tax evasion, and the exporter may receive parallel administrative sanctions under the Customs Act and the Foreign Trade Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with Korean Customs Service for cross-border declaration monitoring
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberal current-account regime but a materially disciplined capital-account framework under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Presidential Decree. The Korean won is not a freely traded offshore currency; inward and outward capital flows require the involvement of a licensed foreign-exchange bank and, for transactions above certain thresholds, a report to the Bank of Korea or the Ministry of Economy and Finance. Current-account payments for royalties, gaming platform commissions and services are generally allowed with documentation, yet the bank is obligated to screen the economic substance of the invoice. Capital-account operations such as equity contributions, loans and acquisitions require a more granular declaration path; non-resident shareholders may inject capital without prior approval in many cases but must route settlement through a domestic local bank and maintain the relevant certificate. Profit remittance to the foreign owner is treated as dividend payment: it is permissible after corporate tax is settled and the foreign-exchange certificate of inward capital is presented, with withholding taxes levied where a treaty rate applies. There is no surrender requirement that forces conversion of export proceeds into KRW; exporters may keep foreign currency in domestic foreign-currency accounts, but settlement of exports and all receipts must be recorded for Bank of Korea statistics.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be collected within 15 months from the export declaration date, unless the exporter obtains a permitted extension or maintains a foreign-currency account with a Korean bank. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; however, if foreign currency is withdrawn or converted, the transaction must be reported to the main foreign-exchange bank and the proceeds are required to be repatriated into a domestic foreign-currency account rather than held indefinitely overseas.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD)
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD)
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI platforms cannot lawfully act as the principal operating bank for a Korean entity; they are not permitted to provide KRW deposit accounts or direct settlement under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act. Such providers may merely facilitate instructions through a licensed Korean bank, and the bank must still perform full KYC on the Chusik Hoesa. Therefore, for core treasury operations, offshore EMIs are not substitutable for a tier-1 Korean commercial bank and their cross-border viability is Low.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors and controlling beneficial owners must effectively present themselves; a physical in-branch interview is mandatory under the Real-Name Financial Transactions Act when opening an operational corporate account. Remote or consular proxy opening is generally rejected for a newly incorporated Chusik Hoesa with non-resident shareholders. Some banks may allow a notarised power of attorney if the principal is physically present on a later visit, but the first onboarding interview is normally an in-person requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO and ownership-chain opacity from non-resident shareholders in a Korean corporation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry extract, Articles of Incorporation, register of shareholders, notarised UBO declaration, passport copies, 3-year biographical background summary, and a source-of-funds statement for each non-resident direct or indirect shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High foreign-currency cash flow profile with substantial incoming App Store/Google Play payouts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed platform agreements with Apple/Google, monthly payout statements, VAT tax invoices and settlement reports, annual audited financial projections, and a cash-flow declaration showing that credits correspond to MMORPG in-app purchases.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border remittance to jurisdictions with enhanced AML supervision or to intermediary payment aggregators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete end-beneficiary chain evidence: invoices or contracts with overseas publishers and operators, payment schedules, SWIFT MT103 records, IP royalty licence agreements, and a written compliance explanation for routing through aggregators.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential mismatch between tax registration status and active commercial substance in Korea.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax clearance certificate or initial tax registration proof, lease or office co-working contract, director's physical presence records, a Korean business plan, and information demonstrating operational substance as a game publisher in Korea.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital for paid-in capital must be remitted through a licensed Korean bank using SWIFT MT103 with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act purpose code for equity investment. The bank will issue a certificate of inward capital remittance which is mandatory for corporate registration and cash settlement. The funds must be kept in a designated foreign-currency account or converted to KRW via the bank's FX desk; any receipt above the report threshold must be reported to the Bank of Korea by the main foreign-exchange bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and service payments should be executed through the treasury bank's SWIFT infrastructure: MT103 for royalties, platform fees and cross-border contractor payments; Commercial Letters of Credit or Documentary Collections for physical game merchandise. Every outbound remittance must be supported by an invoice or contract and, if required, a foreign-exchange settlement report; the bank will screen against OFAC, EU, UN and Korean sanctions lists.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD spot and forward contracts with a licensed Korean bank, limited to underlying trade or investment exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) may be used by non-resident counterparties offshore, but the onshore Chusik Hoesa is normally limited to delivery forwards due to Foreign Exchange Transactions Act regulations
Cross-currency swaps are permitted for genuine economic hedging of foreign-currency liabilities and must be approved within the main bank's FX limit with documented exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return, including the Corporate Tax Base and Tax Payable Declaration with annual financial statements in prescribed HomeTax format
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through HomeTax system; filed at the NTS branch with territorial jurisdiction over the registered head office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year; limited one-month extension is not a general right and requires prescribed grounds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers an additional tax of 20 percent of the assessed corporate income tax for non-filing, 40 percent for underreporting or fraudulent omission; unpaid tax accrues statutory delinquency interest at 3.5 percent per annum from the due date to the payment date; continuous non-compliance leads to compulsory collection, bank seizure, cancellation of business registration, and NTS administrative closure of the entity, which functions as the Korean administrative strike-off trigger.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Return (local surtax return on national corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government, being the Si/Gun/Gu in which the registered head office is located, under the Framework Act on Local Taxation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due simultaneously with the national corporate income tax return within three months after the fiscal year end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underpayment triggers a local additional tax of 20 percent for non-filing and 40 percent for underreporting, plus delinquency interest on unpaid local corporate income tax; prolonged non-payment allows the local government to levy seizure and to request compulsory closure of the business registration and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report of financial statements, when the statutory audit threshold is met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART system; report is also disclosed to the Securities and Futures Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two weeks from delivery of the independent auditor's report to the company and in any event before the regular general shareholders' meeting required to approve the financial statements; the meeting must be held within three months after fiscal year end (by March 31 for a December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor, obtain an audit, or file the audit report subjects the company to statutory fines under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; DART designates the company as an audit non-compliance corporation; repeated non-compliance can trigger regulatory enforcement, suspension of credit rating privileges, restriction of corporate bank operations, and referral for administrative strike-off procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registration of changes in directors, statutory auditor or audit committee members, and representative director in the Commercial Registration Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Korean court registration office, namely the Commercial Registration Office of the local district court or the Supreme Court Registry portal for the head office district
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two weeks of any change in directors, statutory auditor, or representative director; no annual filing is required if no change occurs, but AGM resolutions appointing or re-appointing directors must be registered if the officers change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registration of officer changes is subject to an administrative non-penalty fine of up to KRW 5 million; failure to keep the register current invalidates the company's ability to defend against third-party claims, and the court may, after repeated non-compliance, order dissolution or strike-off under the Commercial Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Regular General Shareholders' Meeting, including approval of audited financial statements and composition of the statutory auditor or audit committee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders through the corporate minute book; no separate government filing is required unless officer changes are registered, but minutes remain a mandatory statutory record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The regular general shareholders' meeting must be convened within three months after the fiscal year end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, by March 31; notice to shareholders must be dispatched at least two weeks before the meeting date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the annual general meeting in time exposes the company and responsible directors to non-penalty fines of up to KRW 10 million under the Commercial Act; absence of properly approved statutory books and minutes can be used as grounds by a court to order dissolution on application by shareholders or creditors, leading to administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, an independent certified CPA audit is compulsory unless the Chusik Hoesa qualifies as a small company. A small company is one that meets all of the following in the immediately preceding fiscal year: total assets below KRW 12,000,000,000; total revenue below KRW 10,000,000,000; and fewer than 300 regular employees. Therefore, a statutory audit is mandatorily triggered by any one of the following quantitative criteria: balance sheet total assets equal to or exceeding KRW 12,000,000,000; total turnover equal to or exceeding KRW 10,000,000,000; or average regular headcount of 300 or more. Publicly listed companies, financial companies, and companies designated by the Financial Services Commission as requiring public disclosure or external audit are audited regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements of an externally audited Chusik Hoesa must be prepared in accordance with Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) if the company is a public-interest entity or is otherwise required to apply K-IFRS; non-public Chusik Hoesa above the audit threshold may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) as adopted by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants. All statutory financial statements must present a true and fair view in Korean won and be accompanied by comparative prior-year figures.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO return is imposed on a private Korean Chusik Hoesa, but the company must maintain a current Register of Shareholders reflecting all share transfers and pledges. Transfers of registered shares are effective against the company only after the acquirer's name, address, and ownership details are entered in the register. For non-resident shareholders, a transfer of shares must be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through a designated foreign exchange bank or the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy within 30 days from the transfer date; annual confirmation of the UBO is instead performed by financial institutions, which, under the Financial Transaction Reports Act, must update and refresh beneficial ownership information for corporate account holders on a risk-based periodic basis. Any resulting change in directors or representative director must be filed with the court registration office within two weeks.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shareholders (Register of Members) with share classes, series, holder details, pledge entries, and transfer records
Register of Statutory Auditor or Audit Committee members
Register of Charges, Mortgages, and Pledge Records
Minute Book of General Shareholders' Meetings
Minute Book of Board of Directors' Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per year for a registered office address and company secretarial agent in Seoul; USD 2,500 - USD 5,000 per year for full Korean registered office, corporate secretarial maintenance, register book upkeep, and coordinated statutory filing support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - USD 28,000 for a private Korean Chusik Hoesa with simple, single-entity operations; USD 30,000 - USD 70,000 for a global MMORPG entity with Apple and Google payout flows, multi-currency transactions, transfer pricing exposure, or K-IFRS consolidated audit requirements.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Progressive 9% (tax base up to KRW 200M), 19% (KRW 200M–20B), 21% (KRW 20B–300B), 24% (over KRW 300B); plus 10% local income surtax, raising the effective headline rate to up to 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credits under Article 10 of the Restriction of Special Taxation Act (up to 30% on qualifying R&D outlays for high-tech game engine development), tax deferral for venture/startup enterprises, and foreign-invested company income tax reductions for high-tech businesses in designated Foreign Investment Zones; no general patent-box regime for software royalties

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (Article 60, Corporate Tax Act), Form No. 1 - 'Base and Calculation of Corporate Tax', filed electronically through HomeTax (national tax e-filing system) with supporting financial statements
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (including a mandatory semi-annual intermediate prepayment filing due within 6 months from the beginning of the current taxable year)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year-end plus 3 months (e.g., for a calendar year, 31 March of the following year); foreign corporations with domestic place of business use the same deadline

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total invoiced consideration for MMORPG game subscriptions, in-app purchases, licensing fees, and service revenue, exclusive of VAT and advance payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize revenue as accrued under the accrual basis; where the enterprise sells through Apple App Store / Google Play top-ups (indirect payment rails), report the gross commission split from the app store operator as service fee income if the Chusik Hoesa is the developer; do not net operating expenses against gross revenue; include foreign-source revenue actually attributable to the Korean company's fixed place of business

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs attributable to game publishing and operation, including server hosting, cloud fees, outsourced development subcontracts, and licensed game engine royalties paid to third parties
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border royalty and subcontract costs paid to non-residents must satisfy the arm's-length standard; expenses reimbursed abroad may be disallowed unless valid contracts, evidence of actual service/use, and tax invoices or reasonable equivalent records are retained; if payments are subject to Korean WHT at source, such WHT must be remitted and reported separately
No special non-resident adjustment; any app-store settlement discounts or chargebacks should be recorded as cost offsets or contra-revenue consistently with Korean GAAP

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Selling, General and Administrative Expenses (SG&A)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating overheads: salaries, marketing/user-acquisition costs, agent commissions, rent, depreciation on office facilities, and legal/accounting fees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenditure incurred abroad for foreign game promotion must be supported by contemporaneous documentation proving economic benefit to the Korean entity; excessive management or intercompany service fees paid to a foreign ultimate parent are subject to TP adjustment and can be reclassified as constructive dividends or capital contributions

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 3 less Box 4; the ordinary profit from ongoing MMORPG publishing activities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean entity has foreign permanent establishments, operating income from those PEs must be reported on the Korean return unless a foreign tax credit or PE exemption applies under a tax treaty

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, dividend income, foreign-exchange gains/losses, disposal gains/losses, impairment losses, and bond issuance or valuation differences
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include passive income flowing from foreign subsidiaries; CFC (controlled foreign company) rules under Article 18 of the International Tax Adjustment Act require aggressive pro-rata inclusion of profits of certain low-taxed foreign subsidiaries unless a statutory exclusion applies; declare foreign tax credits in the supplementary schedule

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income before corporate income tax, computed per the profit-and-loss statement after tax-accounting adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident shareholders, ensure that any fringe benefit or interest-free loan from the Korean company is treated as a constructive dividend subject to WHT under the Corporate Tax Act and reported in the relevant reconciliation schedule

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent differences (non-deductible entertainment, penalties, tariffs) and temporary differences (depreciation, reserves, bad debts) that reconcile book profit to taxable base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deny deductions for foreign bribes or illegal payments; adjust excess loss carryforwards for 10-year utilization with the current statutory rate; preserve evidence for deferred tax asset recognition when cross-border tax losses cannot be supported

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or omission attracts a negligence penalty of 10% of the unpaid tax (or 20% for 'unjustifiable' failure) plus interest of 0.022% per day (the statutory daily surcharge); failure to report an abusive/aggressive tax avoidance scheme can trigger a 40% penalty on the understated amount under the Framework Act on National Taxes; repeated evasion exceeding KRW 300 million in a fiscal year is a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine up to 3 times the evaded tax

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% on gross dividend income paid to non-resident shareholders (plus 2% local income surtax at the aggregate rate of 22%) when the Korean company is the dividend payer
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a lower treaty rate: (i) obtain and submit a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign recipient's competent authority; (ii) complete the Certificate of Resident in a Foreign Country (Form No. 22 of the Income Tax Act) and a withholding-tax exemption/reduction application before or at the time of payment; (iii) provide a beneficial-ownership declaration confirming the recipient is the true owner and receives the dividend not as an intermediary or agent; (iv) if the payer withheld the full 22%, file a refund application with the District Tax Office (or through the HomeTax portal for non-residents) with the TRC, tax invoice, and underlying source evidence. Korea has exchange of information mechanisms for treaty abuse prevention under MLI (Pillar 2) and the Principal Purpose Test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on interest and royalty paid to non-residents is the same 20% plus 2% local surtax (aggregate 22%). Treaty rates generally: royalties on software/commercial income may be reduced to 5%-15% depending on the treaty (e.g., 15% for beneficial owners under the US-Korea treaty, 10% for some jurisdictions; interest often 10%-15%, with widely held institutions eligible for 0% in selected treaties). Industrial-property rights, know-how, and copyright royalties for Game content (including end-user IAP licensing) are taxable to the extent paid in respect of the Korean source; app-store distribution by non-resident platforms may be treated as a separate service, requiring detailed analysis of the OECD/UN Model Commentary.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation are mandatory when intercompany cross-border transactions with a foreign related party exceed KRW 10,000,000,000 per business year; a Master File is required for the consolidated business group with total group revenue of at least KRW 1 trillion; Country-by-Country Report is due for top-tier Korean group entities when the consolidated revenue of the ultimate parent group equals or exceeds KRW 1 trillion (and is exchanged automatically under BEPS Action 13)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea has no separate Economic Substance Regulation comparable to the Cayman regime, but the OECD CIGA analysis is applied in transfer-pricing adjustments and in denying treaty benefits where the recipient has no activation, management, or founders executing development and publishing decisions. The Korean International Tax Adjustment Act and the OECD/UN commentary recognise substance-over-form: shell instructional entities that ring-fence MMORPG IP would not obtain DTA benefits and may be deemed to lack beneficial ownership. The Code of Practice for International Tax Adjustment Act additionally applies the 'place of effective management' test to determine corporate residence and to attack artificially arranged CIGA distributions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsifying MMORPG user revenue streams by booking Apple/Google App-Store refund claims as vendor chargebacks and underreporting in-app purchase proceeds; or deliberately overstating offshore costs for marketing and DevOps services with no actual substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 11-2 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, defrauding the tax authorities is punishable by imprisonment for up to 5 years or a fine of up to 3 times the tax evaded; in addition, the corrected tax is increased by 40% of the understated net amount as an erroneous-report penalty (Article 48 of the Framework Act on National Taxes), plus daily late-payment interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where the director personally signed falsified quarterly reports or used the corporate bank account to transmit evaded profits; civil liability extends to restitution of the tax shortfall and interest from the director's personal assets; criminal conviction produces public blacklisting, a travel ban with involvement of the Immigration Service, and removal from board positions; a sentence of 5 years or more triggers mandatory deportation risk for non-citizen directors

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-Pricing Erosion / Sham Intercompany Transactions (Aggressive Tax Avoidance)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into zero- or low-royalty software licensing and app-store commission split arrangements with a foreign related party pre-arranged to redirect MMORPG profits to a zero-tax jurisdiction, without comparable economic substance or arm's-length compensation for services performed in Korea
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 4 of the International Tax Adjustment Act authorises the National Tax Service to re-determine the taxpayer's income and tax base based on the arm's-length principle; a penalty of 20% of the under-reported net tax (or 30% if the evasion is deemed intentional bet-the-company) applies under the Framework Act provisions; additionally a foreign recipient is treated as a permanent establishment in Korea on arbitrary basis when the substance tests cannot be rebutted
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the sham pricing may be jointly liable for the tax and penalties if the company has been stripped of distributable assets; the court may apply the 'beneficial owner' denial to disallow the reduced treaty rate, exposing the director to an assessment for failure to withhold (WHT plus officer penalty); in extreme cases, intentional use of fabricated documents in an audit leads to criminal charges of obstruction of taxation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Beneficial Ownership Abuse (Anti-Money Laundering and DTA Abuse)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing an opaque foreign holding company (e.g., BVI or HK) with no substantial business presence to receive Korean dividends, royalties, or interest, while the true ultimate beneficial owner remains the Korean developer; the entity fails to prove core income-generating activities and legal substance in the residence jurisdiction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Korean Taxing Authority applies the Principal Purpose Test under Article 7 of the International Tax Adjustment Act (implementing MLI Article 29) to deny treaty benefits, resulting in full 22% withholding plus a 20% erroneous-reporting penalty on the under-withheld amount; the Financial Services Commission's AML sanctions under the Financial Transactions Reports Act impose fines up to KRW 500 million for failure to identify and report beneficial-owner information; the non-resident entity may be blacklisted by the National Tax Service for real ineffective compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who styled the shell as a beneficial owner is a 'de facto director' of the Korean business if the offshore entity has no staff and the director manages all affairs from Seoul; civil isolation and recovery of the tax debt from the director's assets applies under Article 42 of the Framework Act. The framers can also face criminal liability for submitting a false certificate of residence and for aiding tax evasion - punishable by up to 3 years' imprisonment; a travel ban persists until the tax liability and criminal warrant are resolved
